items.stem: What is the optimum temperature of most human enzymes?
items.answer: about 37 °C
items.markingKey: C. Body temperature.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about thermoregulation and the hypothalamus is false?
options: Vasoconstriction is narrowing of arterioles supplying skin capillaries, reducing blood flow near the surface and heat loss.
Brown adipose tissue is fat tissue with many mitochondria that generates heat by uncoupled respiration (thermogenesis).
Thyroxine is a hormone from the thyroid gland that increases metabolic rate and heat production.
Sweat cools you because it is cold.
items.answer: Sweat cools you because it is cold.
items.markingKey: D. The incorrect statement is “Sweat cools you because it is cold.” – Cooling is due to evaporation, which absorbs heat from the skin.

items.stem: Where has atmospheric CO₂ been measured continuously since 1958?
items.answer: Mauna Loa, Hawaii
items.markingKey: D. Charles Keeling began the record.

items.stem: Mass bleaching events in 2016, 2017, 2020, 2022 and 2024 affected large parts of the reef. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (coral bleaching on the Great Barrier Reef)?
items.answer: Effects of climate change
items.markingKey: B. Prolonged high sea temperatures cause corals to expel zooxanthellae, and repeated events prevent recovery.

items.stem: Which statement about continuous variation and polygenic inheritance is not correct?
options: Continuous variation is variation in which a characteristic shows a range of values with no distinct categories, such as height or mass.
Continuous variation is caused only by the environment.
Discontinuous variation is variation in which individuals fall into distinct categories, such as blood groups.
Additive alleles is alleles that each contribute a small, equal amount to the phenotype.
items.answer: Continuous variation is caused only by the environment.
items.markingKey: B. The incorrect statement is “Continuous variation is caused only by the environment.” – It is usually caused by many genes as well as environmental factors.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "disruptive selection"?
options: A species with a disproportionately large effect on community structure, whose removal destabilises the ecosystem
The warming of the Earth’s surface and lower atmosphere because greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit long-wave (infrared) radiation
The production of more offspring than the environment can support, leading to competition and a struggle for survival
Selection that favours both extremes and acts against intermediate phenotypes
items.answer: Selection that favours both extremes and acts against intermediate phenotypes
items.markingKey: D. "disruptive selection" is selection that favours both extremes and acts against intermediate phenotypes.

items.stem: Why is HIV called a retrovirus?
options: It has an RNA genome that is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase.
items.answer: It has an RNA genome that is copied into DNA by reverse transcriptase.
items.markingKey: B. Reverse transcription.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "water potential"?
options: Exchange of sections of chromatids between homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis
The spread of cancer cells from a primary tumour to other parts of the body, forming secondary tumours
Heritable changes in gene expression that do not involve changes to the base sequence of DNA
The potential energy of water per unit volume relative to pure water at atmospheric pressure (ψ, in kPa or MPa); water moves from higher to lower ψ
items.answer: The potential energy of water per unit volume relative to pure water at atmospheric pressure (ψ, in kPa or MPa); water moves from higher to lower ψ
items.markingKey: D. "water potential" is the potential energy of water per unit volume relative to pure water at atmospheric pressure (ψ, in kPa or MPa); water moves from higher to lower ψ.

items.stem: χ² = 11.2 with 3 df (critical 7.81). What is concluded?
options: Reject H₀: significant difference from the expected ratio.
The genes are on different chromosomes.
items.answer: Reject H₀: significant difference from the expected ratio.
items.markingKey: A. χ² > critical.

items.stem: Why are error bars added to graphs of means?
options: They show the variability of the data at each point, helping judge whether differences may be significant.
items.answer: They show the variability of the data at each point, helping judge whether differences may be significant.
items.markingKey: A. Variability.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "metabolic pathway"?
options: The point at which all active sites are occupied, so increasing substrate concentration no longer increases the rate
A molecule with a shape similar to the substrate that binds to the active site, blocking substrate binding
A chain or cycle of enzyme-catalysed reactions in which the product of one reaction is the substrate of the next
The region of an enzyme, formed by a few amino acids, to which the substrate binds and where catalysis occurs
items.answer: A chain or cycle of enzyme-catalysed reactions in which the product of one reaction is the substrate of the next
items.markingKey: C. "metabolic pathway" is a chain or cycle of enzyme-catalysed reactions in which the product of one reaction is the substrate of the next.

items.stem: Which of these statements about sexual and asexual reproduction; human reproductive systems and hormones contains a misconception?
options: Sexual reproduction involves meiosis and fusion of gametes, producing genetically varied offspring.
Asexual reproduction is a primitive process that animals never use.
FSH stimulates follicle growth and oestradiol secretion.
Sexual reproduction is reproduction involving the fusion of haploid gametes from two parents, producing genetically varied offspring.
items.answer: Asexual reproduction is a primitive process that animals never use.
items.markingKey: B. The incorrect statement is “Asexual reproduction is a primitive process that animals never use.” – Many animals reproduce asexually, e.g. aphids by parthenogenesis and Hydra by budding.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A globular protein that acts as a biological catalyst, speeding up a specific reaction without being used up"?
items.answer: enzyme
items.markingKey: B. This is the definition of enzyme.

items.stem: Patients with kidney failure have blood passed through a dialyser with a partially permeable membrane and dialysis fluid. Which concept is best illustrated by this example (kidney dialysis)?
items.answer: Kidney function
items.markingKey: D. Dialysis fluid with normal concentrations of glucose and ions but no urea allows urea and excess ions to diffuse out, replacing filtration.

items.stem: Which of these statements about negative feedback and control of blood glucose by insulin and glucagon contains a misconception?
options: Set point is the normal or target value of a variable that homeostatic mechanisms maintain.
Type 1 diabetes is a condition in which β cells are destroyed by the immune system so little or no insulin is produced.
People with type 2 diabetes produce no insulin.
items.answer: People with type 2 diabetes produce no insulin.
items.markingKey: D. The incorrect statement is “People with type 2 diabetes produce no insulin.” – They usually produce insulin but their cells respond poorly to it.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "systematic error"?
options: How close repeated measurements are to each other
A testable prediction of the relationship between variables, with a scientific explanation
A consistent error in the same direction in all measurements, such as an uncalibrated instrument; not reduced by repeats
A weakness in the method that affects the reliability or validity of the conclusion
items.answer: A consistent error in the same direction in all measurements, such as an uncalibrated instrument; not reduced by repeats
items.markingKey: C. "systematic error" is a consistent error in the same direction in all measurements, such as an uncalibrated instrument; not reduced by repeats.

items.stem: Why is cAMP called a second messenger?
options: It relays the signal from the receptor (first messenger binding) to targets inside the cell.
items.answer: It relays the signal from the receptor (first messenger binding) to targets inside the cell.
items.markingKey: D. Internal relay.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A line across a habitat along which samples are taken at intervals to study changes with an environmental gradient"?
items.answer: transect
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of transect.

items.stem: E. coli with only ¹⁵N DNA were transferred to ¹⁴N medium and allowed to replicate for 3 generations. What fraction of DNA molecules is hybrid (¹⁵N/¹⁴N)?

items.stem: Why are food chains rarely longer than four or five trophic levels?
options: So much energy is lost at each transfer that too little remains to support further levels.
items.answer: So much energy is lost at each transfer that too little remains to support further levels.

items.answer: the pineal gland

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "sexual selection"?
options: An environmental factor, such as predation, disease or competition, that affects the survival and reproduction of individuals with particular traits
Selection arising from competition for mates or mate choice, favouring traits that increase mating success
The principle that allele and genotype frequencies remain constant between generations if there is no selection, mutation, migration or genetic drift and mating is random: p² + 2pq + q² = 1
Differences between individuals that are caused by genes and can be passed on to offspring
items.answer: Selection arising from competition for mates or mate choice, favouring traits that increase mating success
items.markingKey: B. "sexual selection" is selection arising from competition for mates or mate choice, favouring traits that increase mating success.

items.stem: Bacteria lacking the receptor for their own autoinducer are grown at high density. What is expected?

items.answer: They do not show quorum-sensing behaviour such as light production.

items.stem: Which statement about populations: estimating size, sampling and sigmoid growth is not correct?
options: Random sampling is sampling in which every individual or position has an equal chance of being chosen, to avoid bias.
Density-dependent factors (competition, predation, disease) have a greater effect as population density increases and regulate population size.
A population grows exponentially forever if it has enough food.
Lincoln index is the estimate of population size N = M × C / R, where M is the number marked, C the number in the second sample and R the number of marked individuals recaptured.
items.answer: A population grows exponentially forever if it has enough food.
items.markingKey: C. The incorrect statement is “A population grows exponentially forever if it has enough food.” – As the population increases other factors such as space, disease and predation limit it; all populations reach a carrying capacity.

items.stem: Which drug blocks the reuptake of dopamine at synapses?
items.answer: cocaine

items.stem: Which statement about light-dependent and light-independent reactions is not correct?
options: In cyclic photophosphorylation electrons from PSI return to the ETC, producing ATP only.
Photophosphorylation is the production of ATP using energy from light, by chemiosmosis in the thylakoid membrane.
Oxygen comes from the photolysis of water.
The light-independent reactions happen only at night.
items.answer: The light-independent reactions happen only at night.
items.markingKey: D. The incorrect statement is “The light-independent reactions happen only at night.” – They occur in the light (they need ATP and NADPH from the light-dependent reactions); they are “light-independent” because they do not use light directly.

Having the same solute concentration (water potential) as another solution, so there is no net movement of water
A protein whose concentration rises and falls during the cell cycle and which activates cyclin-dependent kinases

items.stem:
Squashes were made of sections of a garlic root taken at different distances from the root tip. The number of cells in mitosis and the total number of cells in a field of view were counted.

Distance from tip / mm | Cells in mitosis | Total cells | Mitotic index
0.5 | 41 | 220 | 0.186
1.0 | 17 | 192 | 0.089
2.0 | 17 | 260 | ?
3.0 | 9 | 212 | 0.042
5.0 | 6 | 249 | 0.024

(a) Calculate the mitotic index at 2.0 mm. [1]
(b) Calculate the percentage change in mitotic index between 0.5 mm and 5.0 mm. [2]
(c) Explain the trend. [2]
(d) Explain why the root tip was treated with hydrochloric acid before staining. [1]
(e) Suggest why a tumour biopsy may have a high mitotic index. [1]
(f) Explain why the root tips were stained before observation. [2]
items.answer: (a) 0.065 (b) -87.1 % (c) The meristem just behind the tip contains actively dividing cells; further back cells elongate and differentiate and stop dividing. (d) Acid breaks down the middle lamella/pectin so cells separate and can be squashed into a single layer. (e) Tumour cells divide uncontrollably, so a higher proportion are in mitosis. (f) Chromosomes are colourless; a stain such as toluidine blue binds DNA so chromosomes are visible and the stage of mitosis can be identified.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] 17/260 = 0.065 (A1). (b) [2] (0.024 − 0.186)/0.186 × 100 (M1) = -87.1 % (A1). (c) [2] Meristem near tip (A1); differentiation further back (A1). (d) [1] Separates cells (A1). (e) [1] Uncontrolled division (A1). (f) [2] Make chromosomes visible (A1); identify the phase (A1).

items.stem:
A student investigated whether sea plantain and thrift are associated in a salt marsh. Presence or absence of each species was recorded in 120 randomly placed quadrats.

 | thrift present | thrift absent
sea plantain present | 21 | 36
sea plantain absent | 52 | 11

(a) State the number of quadrats containing sea plantain. [1]
(b) State a null hypothesis for this investigation. [1]
(c) Calculate the expected number of quadrats containing both species. [2]
(d) Suggest one ecological reason for an association between two plant species. [1]
(e) Explain why quadrats were positioned randomly. [1]
(f) Outline one limitation of using presence or absence data. [1]
(g) Explain why a chi-squared test requires expected values of at least 5 in each cell. [2]
items.answer: (a) 57 (b) There is no association between the distributions of sea plantain and thrift. (c) 34.7 (d) Both prefer the same abiotic conditions (positive) or different conditions/competition/allelopathy (negative); mutualism. (e) To avoid bias so that the sample is representative and the statistical test is valid. (f) It ignores abundance; quadrat size affects results; a single visit may miss seasonal species. (g) With small expected values the χ² statistic is unreliable and the critical values do not apply; more quadrats would be needed.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] 21 + 36 = 57 (A1). (b) [1] No association (A1). (c) [2] 57 × 73/120 (M1) = 34.7 (A1). (d) [1] Valid reason linked to direction (A1). (e) [1] Avoid bias (A1). (f) [1] Valid limitation (A1). (g) [2] Validity of test (A1); more samples needed (A1).

Yeast cells were exposed to different doses of ultraviolet (UV) radiation. The percentage surviving and the number of mutant colonies per 10⁶ surviving cells were recorded.

UV dose / J m⁻² | Survival / % | Mutants per 10⁶ survivors
0 | 100 | 2
10 | 77 | 27
20 | 62 | 51
40 | 38 | 99
80 | 16 | 196

(a) State the number of mutants per 10⁶ survivors at 20 J m⁻². [1]
(b) Calculate how many times greater the mutation frequency is at 40 J m⁻² than with no UV. [1]
(c) Describe the relationship between UV dose and mutation frequency. [2]
(d) Explain why mutants occur even with no UV. [1]
(e) Suggest why human skin cancer risk increases with sun exposure. [1]
(f) Explain why mutation frequency is expressed per 10⁶ surviving cells. [2]
items.answer: (a) 51 (b) 49.5 times (c) Mutation frequency increases with dose, approximately linearly. (d) Spontaneous mutations arise from errors in DNA replication or natural background radiation/chemicals. (e) UV causes mutations in skin cells, including in genes controlling cell division (oncogenes/tumour suppressors), leading to uncontrolled division. (f) Many cells are killed at higher doses, so expressing mutants per survivor allows a fair comparison of mutation rate between doses.
items.markingKey: (a) [1] 51 (A1). (b) [1] 99/2 = 49.5 (A1). (c) [2] Positive (A1); linear/proportional (A1). (d) [1] Spontaneous/replication errors (A1). (e) [1] Mutation in cell-cycle genes (A1). (f) [2] Survival differs between doses (A1); fair comparison (A1).

Pondweed (Elodea) was placed in 1 % sodium hydrogencarbonate solution at 25 °C. A lamp was placed at different distances and the number of bubbles released per minute was counted.

Distance / cm | Relative light intensity (1/d² × 10⁴) | Bubbles per minute

(a) State what is meant by the term "denaturation". [2]

(b) With the help of a specific example, explain the effect of substrate concentration on the rate of an enzyme-catalysed reaction. [4]

(a) Explain the annual and long-term trends shown by the Keeling curve. [2]

(b) The gross primary production of a boreal forest is 2.1 kg m⁻² yr⁻¹ (dry biomass) and plant respiration uses 1.2 kg m⁻² yr⁻¹. Calculate the NPP and the percentage of GPP used in respiration. [4]
